en.name: Capers in brine
en.summary: Capers are flower buds preserved in salt brine or vinegar and sold in small jars. Unopened, a jar keeps about 12 months in a cool dark cupboard. Once opened, refrigerate it and use the capers within about 1–2 months, keeping them under their brine.
en.pantry: An unopened jar keeps about 12 months in a cool, dark cupboard; go by the printed date if it is shorter. Salt and acid are what preserve capers, so no refrigeration is needed while the jar is sealed. Keep it away from the hob and out of direct sunlight, and do not store a jar whose lid has lost its vacuum. Salt-packed capers, sold buried in dry salt rather than in liquid, are a different product and keep in the cupboard too — rinse and soak them before use.
en.fridge: Once opened, refrigerate at 4 °C (40 °F) or below and use within about 1–2 months. The single habit that matters is keeping the capers submerged: any that sit proud of the liquid dry out and go mouldy first. Use a clean fork, never your fingers, and if the level drops top the jar up with brine or a little vinegar rather than water, which dilutes the very thing doing the preserving. No source publishes a figure for capers by name, so these numbers come from the general lines for unopened canned foods and for opened pickles and olives.
en.freezer: There is no freezer timeline for capers, and freezing them is pointless: they are already a preserve, they keep for months in the fridge, and freezing turns a firm bud soft and hollow. If a jar is outliving your appetite for it, buy the smallest size next time or start using capers in more places — they are good well beyond puttanesca, in butter sauces, potato salads and anything fried.
spoilage: Mould on the surface or on any buds standing above the brine
Brine gone cloudy, ropy or slimy
A rotten or yeasty smell rather than a sharp, salty, faintly floral one
Buds gone mushy or falling apart between the fingers
tips: Always press the capers back under the brine before closing the jar.
Use a clean fork, never fingers.
Top up with brine or vinegar, not water.
Buy small jars if you only cook with capers occasionally.

faq.q: Do capers need to be refrigerated after opening?
faq.a: Yes. Refrigerate at 4 °C or below and use within about 1–2 months, keeping the buds under their brine.

faq.q: How long do unopened capers last?
faq.a: About 12 months in a cool dark cupboard, or the printed date if that is sooner.
There is no timeline and no need. They already keep for months refrigerated, and freezing makes them soft and hollow.

faq.q: Why did the capers on top go mouldy?
faq.a: Because they were above the brine. Anything not submerged dries out and moulds first, so push them back under each time.

zh.name: 酸豆
zh.summary: 酸豆是用鹽水或醋醃漬保存的花蕾，通常以小玻璃罐販售。未開封放在陰涼避光的櫥櫃大約 12 個月。開封後請冷藏，並在大約 1～2 個月內用完，過程中要讓它一直泡在醃汁裡。
zh.pantry: 未開封的罐子放在陰涼避光的櫥櫃大約 12 個月；如果瓶身標示的日期更短，就以標示為準。保存酸豆的是鹽和酸，所以只要密封完好就不需要冷藏。請遠離爐火、避免日曬，蓋子已經沒有真空感的罐子就不要再存放。另有一種埋在乾鹽裡販售的鹽漬酸豆，那是不同的產品，同樣放櫥櫃，使用前要沖洗、泡水去鹽。
zh.fridge: 開封後請放 4 °C 以下，並在大約 1～2 個月內用完。最重要的習慣只有一個：讓酸豆完全泡在液面以下；露出液面的那些會先乾掉、先發霉。請用乾淨的叉子，不要用手；液面下降就補鹽水或一點醋，不要補清水——清水會稀釋掉真正在保存它的東西。沒有來源特別為酸豆公布數字，這裡的數字取自「未開封罐頭食品」與「開封後的醃菜與橄欖」這兩條通則。
zh.freezer: 酸豆沒有冷凍期限，冷凍也沒有意義：它本來就是醃漬保存品，冷藏可以放好幾個月，而冷凍會讓原本結實的花蕾變軟、變空。如果一罐老是用不完，下次買最小罐，或把它用在更多地方——除了煙花女義大利麵，奶油醬汁、馬鈴薯沙拉和各種炸物都很搭。
spoilage: 液面或露出液面的花蕾長霉
醃汁變濁、出現絲狀物或黏稠感
聞起來是腐敗味或酵母味，而不是嗆鹹帶淡淡花香
tips: 蓋回去之前，先把酸豆壓回醃汁裡。
用乾淨的叉子，不要用手。
液面不夠時補鹽水或醋，不要補清水。
偶爾才用的話，請買小罐。

faq.a: 要。放 4 °C 以下冷藏，並在大約 1～2 個月內用完，全程讓花蕾泡在醃汁裡。

faq.q: 未開封的酸豆可以放多久？
faq.a: 陰涼避光的櫥櫃大約 12 個月，若瓶身日期更早則以日期為準。
沒有對應期限，也沒有必要。它冷藏就能放好幾個月，冷凍反而會變軟變空。

faq.q: 上層的酸豆為什麼發霉了？
faq.a: 因為它露出液面。沒泡到醃汁的會先乾掉、先長霉，每次用完都把它們壓回去。
